interface.signature: logistic_map(width: int, height: int, x_coords: list[int], y_coords: list[int]) -> list[list[int | None]]

preconditions.description: The map dimensions (width and height) must be positive integers.
The lists of x and y coordinates for supply points must have the same length.

preconditions.expression: all(0 <= x < width for x in x_coords) and all(0 <= y < height for y in y_coords)
preconditions.description: All supply point coordinates must lie within the map boundaries (inclusive of 0, exclusive of width/height).

postconditions.expression: len(return_value) == height and all(len(row) == width for row in return_value)
postconditions.description: The output is a 2D list with dimensions matching the input width and height.

postconditions.expression: all(x_coords and y_coords or all(cell is None for row in return_value for cell in row))
postconditions.description: If there are no supply points, every cell in the output is `None`; otherwise, every cell contains an integer representing the Manhattan distance to the nearest supply point.

postconditions.expression: all(0 <= i < height and 0 <= j < width and (return_value[i][j] is None or return_value[i][j] == min(abs(i - y) + abs(j - x) for x, y in zip(x_coords, y_coords))) for i in range(height) for j in range(width))
postconditions.description: For each cell (i, j) in the output, if there are supply points, the value is the minimum Manhattan distance to any supply point (|i - y| + |j - x| for each supply point (x, y)).
